title: Next.js 15
authorityNotes: Official Next.js release announcement. Supports claims about Next.js 15 requirements and router-specific React support.

title: How to upgrade to version 15
authorityNotes: Official version 15 upgrade guide. Covers 14-to-15 upgrade behavior and requirements.

title: How to upgrade to version 16
authorityNotes: Official version 16 upgrade guide. Covers 15-to-16 upgrade behavior and requirements.

title: Next.js 15.1
authorityNotes: Official Next.js 15.1 announcement. Describes stable React 19 support in both routers and continued React 18 support in Pages Router.

title: React 19 Upgrade Guide
authorityNotes: Official React upgrade guide; React 19 install instructions specify matching react and react-dom major versions and updated types.

title: React v19
authorityNotes: Official stable React 19 release announcement; includes React DOM release information and a link to the upgrade guide.

title: Node.js Releases
authorityNotes: Official release-line schedule, lifecycle state, and dates. These values are time-sensitive.

title: Node.js End-of-Life
authorityNotes: Official explanation of EOL consequences and EOL release lines.

title: TypeScript 5.1 Release Notes
authorityNotes: Official TypeScript release notes. Establishes TypeScript version existence/date, not Next.js compatibility.

title: React 19.2
authorityNotes: Official React 19.2 release announcement; used with Next.js 16's statement that its App Router Canary includes React 19.2 features.

statement: Next.js 15 requires Node.js 18.18.0 or later.
sourceEvidence: The release announcement lists: “The minimum required Node.js version has been updated to 18.18.0.”

statement: Next.js 16 requires Node.js 20.9.0 or later; Node.js 18 is no longer supported.
sourceEvidence: Runtime support table: “Node.js 20.9+” and “Minimum version now 20.9.0 (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported.”

statement: The Next.js 16 upgrade guide lists TypeScript 5.1.0 as the minimum version.
sourceEvidence: Runtime support table: “TypeScript 5+” with details “Minimum version now 5.1.0.”

statement: The Next.js 15 upgrade guide specifies React 19 as the minimum for its documented upgrade path; the Next.js 15 release announcement separately documents a React 18 exception for Pages Router.
sourceEvidence: Version 15 upgrade guide: minimum versions of react and react-dom are 19. Next.js 15 announcement: Pages Router maintains backward compatibility with React 18.

statement: The Next.js 15 upgrade guide specifies React DOM 19 as the minimum for its documented upgrade path; the Next.js 15 release announcement separately documents a React 18 exception for Pages Router.
sourceEvidence: Version 15 upgrade guide: minimum versions of react and react-dom are 19. Next.js 15 announcement: Pages Router maintains backward compatibility with React 18.

title: Next.js 15 Pages Router supports React 18
condition: Pages Router. The Next.js 15.1 announcement explicitly says Pages Router continues to support React 18.
statement: Next.js 15 maintains backward compatibility for the Pages Router with React 18; Next.js 15.1 says Pages Router continues to support React 18 alongside React 19 stable.
sourceEvidence: Next.js 15 release: “Next.js 15 maintains backward compatibility for the Pages Router with React 18.” Next.js 15.1: Pages Router can use React 19 stable “alongside continued support for React 18.”

title: Next.js 15.1 supports React 19 across both routers
condition: Next.js 15.1. Pages Router can use React 19 stable; App Router continues to use built-in React Canary releases that include stable React 19 changes and newer framework-validated features.
statement: Next.js 15.1 announces React 19 stable support in both routers, while describing the App Router's built-in React Canary behavior separately.
sourceEvidence: Next.js 15.1 release notes: React 19 stable may be used in the Pages Router; the App Router continues to provide React Canary releases that include all stable React 19 changes and newer framework-validated features.

title: React upgrade uses matching React and React DOM major
condition: React 19 installation path in the React 19 upgrade guide.
statement: The React 19 upgrade guide recommends installing React 19 and React DOM 19 together.
sourceEvidence: Install instructions: `react@^19.0.0 react-dom@^19.0.0`.

title: Proxy does not support Edge runtime in Next.js 16
condition: When migrating middleware to proxy, a proxy configured to use Edge runtime is unsupported.
statement: The Next.js 16 proxy runtime is Node.js and cannot be configured; Edge runtime is not supported in proxy.
sourceEvidence: The upgrade guide states: “The edge runtime is NOT supported in proxy. The proxy runtime is nodejs, and it cannot be configured.”

title: Next.js 16 App Router uses React Canary with React 19.2 features
condition: App Router only; Next.js documents its latest React Canary with React 19.2 features and incremental stabilization. This does not establish an exact stable React/React DOM package version for every deployment.
statement: The Next.js 16 upgrade guide states that the App Router uses the latest React Canary, which includes the newly released React 19.2 features.
sourceEvidence: Next.js 16 upgrade guide, section “React 19.2”: “The App Router in Next.js 16 uses the latest React Canary release, which includes the newly released React 19.2 features.”

title: Node.js 20 meets the Next.js 16 floor but is EOL
condition: Node.js 20.9 or later meets Next.js 16's stated minimum; as of the Node.js Releases page retrieved 2026-10-04, the Node.js 20 major line is EOL. Framework minimum satisfaction does not imply currently maintained runtime status.
statement: Next.js 16's Node.js 20.9 minimum is met by the Node.js 20 line, but the Node.js project lists Node.js 20 as EOL as of this dataset's retrieval date.
sourceEvidence: Next.js 16 guide lists Node.js 20.9+ as the minimum. Node.js Releases page lists v20 status as EOL; retrieved 2026-10-04.

title: Node.js 18 support removed in Next.js 16
statement: Next.js 16 raises the minimum Node.js version to 20.9.0 and no longer supports Node.js 18.
sourceEvidence: Runtime support table: “Node.js 20.9+” and “Node.js 18 no longer supported.”

title: Middleware convention renamed to Proxy in Next.js 16
statement: The middleware filename and named export are deprecated and renamed to proxy; the upgrade guide supplies the rename and notes the Edge runtime caveat.
sourceEvidence: Section “middleware to proxy”: filename and export rename instructions; “The edge runtime is NOT supported in proxy.”

title: Dynamic request APIs became asynchronous in Next.js 15
statement: Next.js 15 changes cookies, headers, draftMode, params, and searchParams APIs from synchronous access to asynchronous APIs, with a codemod and temporary synchronous access path documented.
sourceEvidence: Section “Async Request APIs”: lists cookies, headers, draftMode, params, and searchParams; says a codemod and temporary synchronous access are available.

title: React 19 removes ReactDOM.render
statement: React 19 removes ReactDOM.render; applications using it must migrate to createRoot from react-dom/client.
sourceEvidence: React 19 Upgrade Guide, “Removed: ReactDOM.render”: ReactDOM.render is removed in React 19 and directs users to ReactDOM.createRoot.

title: Next.js 16 makes sitemap id asynchronous
statement: Starting with Next.js 16, the id passed to a sitemap generating function is a Promise and must be awaited before use.
sourceEvidence: Next.js 16 upgrade guide, “Async id parameter for sitemap”: the id is now Promise<string> and the example awaits it.

title: Upgrade Node.js for Next.js 16
steps: Use Node.js 20.9.0 or later for Next.js 16.
statement: The Next.js 16 upgrade guide sets Node.js 20.9.0 as the minimum; this migration step is satisfied by a declared Node.js version at or above that threshold.
sourceEvidence: The guide's runtime support table sets Node.js minimum version to 20.9.0.

title: Rename middleware to proxy
steps: Rename middleware.ts or middleware.js to proxy.ts or proxy.js.
Rename the named export middleware to proxy.
Review runtime use: proxy uses Node.js runtime; Edge runtime is not supported in proxy.
statement: The Next.js 16 upgrade guide documents renaming middleware files and exports to proxy and states that Edge runtime is not supported in proxy.
sourceEvidence: Section “middleware to proxy” contains the two rename instructions and states proxy runtime is nodejs and cannot be configured; edge is not supported.

title: Migrate to asynchronous request APIs
steps: Await params and searchParams where documented.
Use the provided codemod or documented temporary synchronous compatibility access where required.
statement: The Next.js 15 upgrade guide documents the APIs becoming asynchronous and provides codemod and temporary synchronous access guidance.
sourceEvidence: Async API section shows before/after examples such as `await cookies()` and describes a codemod and temporary synchronous compatibility casts.

title: Migrate ReactDOM.render to createRoot
steps: Replace ReactDOM.render with createRoot from react-dom/client.
Render through the root returned by createRoot.
statement: The React 19 Upgrade Guide directs applications using ReactDOM.render to migrate to createRoot.
sourceEvidence: React 19 Upgrade Guide shows the before/after migration from render imported from react-dom to createRoot imported from react-dom/client.

title: Await the sitemap id in Next.js 16
steps: Treat the sitemap generating function's id parameter as a Promise.
Await id before converting or using it.
statement: The Next.js 16 upgrade guide's before/after example changes synchronous id access to awaiting the id Promise.
sourceEvidence: Next.js 16 guide: `const resolvedId = await id`; id is now Promise<string>.

title: React 18 is supported in Next.js 15 Pages Router
condition: The application uses the Pages Router. This exception does not establish React 18 compatibility for the App Router.
effect: Next.js 15 (including the 15.1 announcement) retains Pages Router support for React 18.
sourceEvidence: Next.js 15 release announcement explicitly says Pages Router is backward compatible with React 18 and warns against mixed router React versions. Next.js 15.1 says Pages Router continues to support React 18.

title: Keep middleware when the Edge runtime is required
condition: The existing middleware depends on the Edge runtime.
effect: Do not migrate that middleware to proxy on the assumption that Edge is supported; the Next.js 16 guide says proxy runs on Node.js and advises keeping middleware to continue using Edge.
sourceEvidence: Next.js 16 upgrade guide, “middleware to proxy”: Edge runtime is not supported in proxy; to continue using Edge, keep using middleware.
